S No  Registrar's order with  Signatures  22.03.2023  C482 No. 486 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Vaibhav Singh Chauhan, Advocate, for the applicant.
Mr. Pankaj Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State.
Mr. Pranav Singh, Advocate, for the complainant.

This C482 Application arises out of an FIR, being FIR No. 357 of 2021, dated 28.08.2021, which was initially got registered against the present applicant, for his alleged involvement in commission of offence under Sections 354, 376, 504, 511 of IPC, as well as Section 3(1)(s) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, which was registered against him at P.S.
Jhabrera, District Haridwar.

entities.text: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On culmination of investigation, the Chargesheet, being Chargesheet No. 1 of 2021 dated 24.10.2021, was submitted as against the present applicant, wherein the offence under Sections 354 and Section 504 of IPC was shown to have been made out against him.
Accordingly, he has been summoned by an order dated 07.01.2022, by the Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar in Special Sessions Trial No. 4 of 2022, State Vs. Jaan Alam.

entities.text: Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Special Sessions Trial No. 4 of 2022, State Vs. Jaan Alam
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said offence is sought to be compounded by filing the Compounding Application (IA/1/2023), which has been duly signed by all the parties, including their respective counsel.
The parties are present in person.
This Court has interacted with the complainant, as well as the applicant accused.
In fact, the applicant accused has sought an apology, by submitting that he may be forgiven for the offences which has been complained of against him in the FIR.

This in itself will amount, that it is an admission by the applicant, that he has committed an offence and in Criminal Law, the apology doesn't have any scope or place, to accept the forgiveness, to be given by the complainant to the applicant accused.

The learned Government Advocate opposes the Compounding Application, on the ground, that since the offence under Section 354 of IPC is not compoundable under Section 320 of CrPC.

But, in order to balance the equity, while exercising my inherent powers under Section 482 of CrPC and in order to bring tranquillity amongst the parties to the proceedings, who are residents of same place, the proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No. 4 of 2022, State Vs. Jaan Alam, pending consideration before the Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar, would hereby stand dropped, subject to the condition that the applicant accused remits an amount of penalty of Rs.
50,000/- to be herein within 2 weeks, so that it may be creating as a deterrent to the applicant, as well as the other similar persons, for not to engage themselves in such type of anti- social offences,
as against the females.

entities.text: Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Subject to payment of Rs. 50,000/- to the complainant respondent No. 3 herein, within 2 weeks, by the applicant, the proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No. 4 of 2022, State Vs. Jaan Alam, pending consideration before the Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar, would hereby stand dropped.

entities.text: Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the present C482 Application would stand disposed of subject to the aforesaid terms.

(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 22.03.2023 Mahinder/

opennyai_summary.facts:
This C482 Application arises out of an FIR, being FIR No. 357 of 2021, dated 28.08.2021, which was initially got registered against the present applicant, for his alleged involvement in commission of offence under Sections 354, 376, 504, 511 of IPC, as well as Section 3(1)(s) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, which was registered against him at P.S.
Jhabrera, District Haridwar.
On culmination of investigation, the Chargesheet, being Chargesheet No. 1 of 2021 dated 24.10.2021, was submitted as against the present applicant, wherein the offence under Sections 354 and Section 504 of IPC was shown to have been made out against him.
In fact, the applicant accused has sought an apology, by submitting that he may be forgiven for the offences which has been complained of against him in the FIR.
The learned Government Advocate opposes the Compounding Application, on the ground, that since the offence under Section 354 of IPC is not compoundable under Section 320 of CrPC.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: This in itself will amount, that it is an admission by the applicant, that he has committed an offence and in Criminal Law, the apology doesn't have any scope or place, to accept the forgiveness, to be given by the complainant to the applicant accused.
opennyai_summary.decision:
But, in order to balance the equity, while exercising my inherent powers under Section 482 of CrPC and in order to bring tranquillity amongst the parties to the proceedings, who are residents of same place, the proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No. 4 of 2022, State Vs. Jaan Alam, pending consideration before the Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar, would hereby stand dropped, subject to the condition that the applicant accused remits an amount of penalty of Rs.
50,000/- to be herein within 2 weeks, so that it may be creating as a deterrent to the applicant, as well as the other similar persons, for not to engage themselves in such type of anti- social offences,
as against the females.
Subject to payment of Rs. 50,000/- to the complainant respondent No. 3 herein, within 2 weeks, by the applicant, the proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No. 4 of 2022, State Vs. Jaan Alam, pending consideration before the Court of Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Haridwar, would hereby stand dropped.
Accordingly, the present C482 Application would stand disposed of subject to the aforesaid terms.
